description: The dotnet CLI's pack switches on an asm library and an asm .NET tool, and the package and tool commands that use what they make: the version, version-suffix, symbol, source and no-build forms of pack (the scenarios' Directory.Build.props sets PackageOutputPath, so an artifacts path would not move a package here; CliBuild moves builds with one); dotnet package add, list and remove with dotnet nuget why from a C# app under central package management; a tool packed with its PackageId on the command line, and a local tool manifest, dotnet tool run, the tool's own dotnet command and dotnet tool exec.

steps.description: The library's package, into the local feed the scenarios' nuget.config maps Scenario.* to; it covers the eight native RIDs, so the pack gives no ASM0013 (a warning, which TreatWarningsAsErrors leaves a warning).
The version switch replaces the whole version.
The version-suffix switch adds a suffix to the project's VersionPrefix.
A .snupkg holds portable PDBs, which an asm package has none of: the package is made, the symbol package is not, and the pack says why (0.4.0 wrote an empty .snupkg, which nuget.org refuses).
The include-source switch makes NuGet's legacy symbols package, with the sources under src/.
Packs the Release build the first step made, without building again.
Adds the package to the C# app; under central package management the version goes to Directory.Packages.props.
The package brings the library of this machine's RID and the C# bindings.
NuGet explains the dependency from the restore of the asm package.
The tool's top-level package and the package of each RID.

With the PackageId on the command line, a global property, each RID package still gets <id>.<rid> (0.4.0 gave every RID package the top-level id, and the packs wrote the same file at once: being used by another process).
One RID's package alone cannot take its RID suffix from a PackageId on the command line: ASM0056 says what to do instead.
A local tool manifest in the scenario's folder.

steps.run: dotnet tool run asm-echo -- a "b c"
steps.description: dotnet tool run starts this machine's program with the arguments as given: it prints each and returns their number.
A local tool's own dotnet command.
dotnet tool exec (what dnx runs) installs nothing and runs the package the command-line PackageId made: its RID packages are named and found.
